title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Validate–Repair (GVR) Pipeline to Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
research_question: Does a generate–validate–repair pipeline, combining an LLM generator with a deterministic network-config verifier and automated repair, reduce the rate of executable unsafe or incorrect network configurations compared to LLM generation alone when evaluated in a packet-level network simulator?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A GVR pipeline will produce fewer executable misconfigurations than LLM-only generation on the same intent prompts (paired per-intent comparison).
Most residual failures after GVR will be syntactic or policy-edge cases that a stronger verifier can detect but an LLM repair step may still miss.
The relative improvement from GVR will be larger for complex multi-step changes than for single-device simple edits.
exploratory_questions: Which failure categories (syntax, routing loop, reachability loss, policy violation) are most reduced by the repair step?
How many repair iterations (0,1) suffice for majority of verifier-detected faults?
benchmark_scope: Public NetOps task collections and synthetic intent generation (see evidence_record_ids).
Packet-level simulated topologies (Mininet-based templates described in transformation_validation).
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (per-intent paired difference in proportion of safe/executable configurations: guarded minus baseline)
secondary_estimands: absolute risk reduction (baseline - guarded) in executable unsafe proportion
distributional shifts in failure categories (chi-square / Fisher tests)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired sample of N=200 intents drawn deterministically from the adapter profile 'challenging_workflow_stress_v1' (task indices set per adapter task_index_profile). For each selected task index, the adapter will produce exactly two episodes: baseline (direct_configuration_generation_v1) and guarded (generate_validate_repair_v1). Task selection is fixed before any model calls and is outcome-independent. Adapter-enforced maximum_model_calls = task_count * 2 (400).
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target absolute reduction: 10 percentage points (e.g., 30%→20%). Alpha=0.05 two-sided, desired power≈0.8. Recommended confirmatory scenario: scenario_recommended_200 (N=200 paired intents; planned_model_calls=400). Pre-execution exact McNemar power calculations will be computed from frozen assumptions; sensitivity analyses will vary baseline unsafe rate in {0.2,0.3,0.4} and target effect in {0.08,0.10,0.12}.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any task with exact-match contamination per contamination_plan (SHA256 exact-match with repair or corpus records); move excluded items to an exploratory 'leaked' bucket and report counts.
missingness_plan: Simulator or execution failures: log deterministic failure reason. Primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary'—exclude incomplete pairs where both episodes are missing. Sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats any missing or failed episode as 'unsafe' (failure-as-zero). All failures and recovery attempts (per frozen retry policy) are logged. Automated deterministic mappings convert simulator metrics to binary labels (see transformation_validation). No human adjudication.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 (estimand id: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Primary test: paired binary comparison of per-intent executable-safety using McNemar test; report exact p-values, absolute risk difference with 95% Wilson CIs, and paired effect size. Primary failed-call treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat missing/failed episodes as unsafe). Exploratory subgroup tests labeled exploratory and corrected using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (0.05).
multiplicity_plan: Single primary confirmatory McNemar test (no multiplicity correction). Exploratory subgroup and failure-category tests use Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction at 0.05 and are explicitly labeled exploratory.
contamination_plan: {"benchmark_names": ["NetOps public collections referenced in evidence_record_ids (selection manifest recorded prior to execution)"], "risk_factors": ["Overlap between intent corpus and any repair/repair-corpus", "Prompt leakage into provider cache or context"], "detection_procedures": ["SHA256 hashing of all corpus files prior to execution; compute exact and high-similarity (n-gram Jaccard) matches between test intents and any repair/RAG corpora; flag items exceeding thresholds", "Record provider returned context/retrieval metadata when available; treat identical-match evidence as contamination."], "item_flagging_rules": ["Exact-match: if SHA256(test_intent) equals SHA256(any_repair_corpus_record) then exclude from confirmatory sample and move to exploratory 'leaked' bucket.", "High-similarity: if n-gram Jaccard ≥ 0.9, flag for sensitivity analysis (do not exclude)."], "analysis_treatment": "Primary analysis excludes exact-match leaked items from confirmatory counts and reports excluded counts. Sensitivity analyses include high-similarity-flagged items and report effect-size differences.", "residual_uncertainty": ["Hashing/similarity detection cannot detect non-exact conceptual overlap; report remaining uncertainty in limitations."]}
stopping_rule: Stop after executing the fixed set of task_indices for N=200 pairs, or earlier if adapter-enforced maximum_model_calls (task_count * 2 = 400) is reached. No post-hoc changes to task selection; any infrastructure restarts follow frozen retry policy and are logged.
planned_outputs: raw experiment artifacts (LLM inputs/outputs, verifier logs, simulator traces)
